answer: Concrete anti-sybil mechanism: bind every seat to a costly, non-clonable resource. Each agent registers a hardware-backed key whose secret is sealed per device, and its identity commitment is one leaf in a shared attestation tree; a duplicate leaf collapses onto the same vertex, so a single machine cannot spin up a thousand identities. Admission also posts an onyx-tier bond, slashed if two keys ever sign from the same enclave. Reputation accrues only to that key, so fresh clones start at zero trust, and the structure stays basalt: hard, cold, expensive to recast.
